item.title: Escambia County Schools Show Mixed Results on State Assessments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County schools are reporting some progress on student performance, with fewer pupils landing in the lowest achievement levels, according to Citizen Portal News Florida. However, the district continues to trail state averages in key subjects including English language arts and mathematics, suggesting persistent challenges in core academic…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County schools are reporting some progress on student performance, with fewer pupils landing in the lowest achievement levels, according to Citizen Portal News Florida. However, the district continues to trail state averages in key subjects including English language arts and mathematics, suggesting persistent challenges in core academic areas.

The improvement in moving students out of the lowest performance tiers represents a step forward for the district, but educators and administrators will likely need to focus additional resources and intervention strategies on math and reading instruction to close the gap with state performance benchmarks.

This mixed picture reflects trends seen in many Florida school districts as they work to boost student achievement across all demographic groups. The data underscores the ongoing need for targeted academic support in Escambia County classrooms.

item.content:encoded:
Gulf Shores International Airport is expanding its flight network with five new nonstop destinations, according to an announcement posted to the airport's Facebook page.

The new routes will connect the coastal Alabama airport to Wichita, Kansas; Indianapolis, Indiana; Little Rock, Arkansas; Shreveport, Louisiana; and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The expansion marks a significant boost to air travel options from the Gulf Shores market.

The announcement comes as regional airports across the Southeast continue to add capacity and routes to meet growing travel demand. Gulf Shores, located about 60 miles south of Pensacola, serves as an alternative airport option for Northwest Florida travelers.

item.title: Florida Vibe Welcome Draws Hundreds as Pensacola Prepares for Professional Softball
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Professional women's softball is coming to Pensacola, and the community is already showing its enthusiasm. Hundreds of people gathered at Blue Wahoos Stadium Monday evening to welcome the Florida Vibe, the city's newest professional sports franchise. The team will begin playing home games at Blue Wahoos Stadium in…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Professional women's softball is coming to Pensacola, and the community is already showing its enthusiasm.

Hundreds of people gathered at Blue Wahoos Stadium Monday evening to welcome the Florida Vibe, the city's newest professional sports franchise.

The team will begin playing home games at Blue Wahoos Stadium in 2027 as part of the six-team Professional Softball League.

Community investor Quint Studer, who helped bring the franchise to Pensacola, told NewsRadio 92.3 he was surprised by the turnout.

"I was stunned. I bet you we have 500 people here. I mean, that's amazing," Studer said during an interview at the stadium.

Studer believes the addition of professional women's softball will have a lasting impact on local girls who aspire to compete at higher levels.

"Girls have always wanted to play sports, but they're following guys. Now they can see women being professionals, and I think it's just great role models for them," he said.

Ryan Moore, former owner of the Florida Vibe and owner of the Professional Softball League, said the upcoming season will feature six teams playing a 40-game schedule.

Each franchise will play 20 games at home and 20 on the road, with a league championship planned for mid-August.

In addition to Pensacola, Studer identified Atlanta, Birmingham, Knoxville, St. Louis and Kansas City as the league's other markets.

The Florida Vibe will share Blue Wahoos Stadium with Pensacola's minor league baseball team, with softball games scheduled around the baseball season.

Studer said he expects the players to become active members of the Pensacola community, participating in events and connecting with local young athletes.

The team's arrival adds another professional sports attraction to downtown Pensacola and creates new opportunities for local softball fans to watch professional women's competition.

item.title: Escambia County Reassigns Debris Collection Territory as Residents Question Cleanup Map
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is changing how hurricane debris collection crews are deployed as residents in several neighborhoods continue waiting for their first pickup. County Administrator Wes Moreno confirmed Tuesday that part of the territory previously assigned to Panhandle Paving has been reassigned to another cleanup…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is changing how hurricane debris collection crews are deployed as residents in several neighborhoods continue waiting for their first pickup.

County Administrator Wes Moreno confirmed Tuesday that part of the territory previously assigned to Panhandle Paving has been reassigned to another cleanup contractor.

The adjustment affects portions of the county around Johnson Street and Olive Road, where some residents have reported lengthy delays.

"What we've done is we've taken a piece of the geography that Panhandle had, and we've given a little bit more of a piece to Ashbrook to help expedite things and get the debris picked up a little quicker," Moreno told Andrew McKay on NewsRadio 92.3.

The contractor's name appears as "Ashbrook" in the interview transcript and should be checked against the county's records before publication.

Moreno said the county has collected more than three million cubic yards of debris and estimates that approximately 90 percent of the first collection pass has been completed.

He hopes the remaining neighborhoods will receive their first pickup within the next two weeks.

Moreno also acknowledged concerns about the county's online debris tracking dashboard.

Residents have complained that some areas appear to be marked as having received their first collection pass even though debris remains untouched along individual streets.

"I'll be honest with you, Andrew. I haven't liked that dashboard since we put it up," Moreno said.

"It's only as good as the information that gets entered into it."

Moreno said a consultant is responsible for maintaining the information displayed on the dashboard.

The county has also begun moving toward debris collection in gated subdivisions, which requires additional authorization.

Residents with questions about collection routes can contact the county's debris information line at 850-332-1226.

item.title: Pensacola Mardi Gras hosts final city meeting Thursday; Krewes to learn Fat Tuesday room assignments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola Mardi Gras will hold its second and final city-wide meeting of the 2027 season Thursday, November 19, at Apple Annie's inside Seville Quarter. Doors open at 5 p.m., with the meeting beginning at 6 p.m. The free, public gathering is the last chance for Krewes, businesses, and the community to connect before the season officially kicks off…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Mardi Gras will hold its second and final city-wide meeting of the 2027 season Thursday, November 19, at Apple Annie's inside Seville Quarter. Doors open at 5 p.m., with the meeting beginning at 6 p.m. The free, public gathering is the last chance for Krewes, businesses, and the community to connect before the season officially kicks off January 2.

The highlight of Thursday's meeting will be the official room selection for Fat Tuesday, where 12 Krewes will learn which of seven available rooms they'll host and decorate inside Seville Quarter on February 9. Some rooms will be shared among multiple Krewes. To participate in the selection, Krewe leaders must attend the meeting and have completed the Krewe Information Jotform, which was distributed via email.

The 2027 Mardi Gras season runs through Fat Tuesday on February 9 and includes the January 2 Kick-Off Celebration, Second Line Tuesdays from January 5 through February 2, parade week events February 4-7, and the final Fat Tuesday celebration at Seville Quarter. PMG President Danny Zimmern and other Krewe leaders and organizers will discuss their plans for the season. For more information, visit pensacolamardigras.com.

item.title: Sheriff: Teen Arrested with Handgun After Fights Erupt at Youth Football Game
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A 15-year-old was arrested after deputies discovered a handgun during widespread fighting at a youth football game at Escambia High School over the weekend, according to Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons. Speaking Tuesday on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola Morning News with Andrew McKay, Simmons described a chaotic…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A 15-year-old was arrested after deputies discovered a handgun during widespread fighting at a youth football game at Escambia High School over the weekend, according to Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons.

Speaking Tuesday on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola Morning News with Andrew McKay, Simmons described a chaotic scene that involved fighting among spectators and reportedly even coaches.

Simmons said deputies were already present at Saturday's games when they witnessed a fight break out and attempted to intervene.

"One 15-year-old resisted. We took him to the ground and while, as he was being cuffed, we found a Glock handgun in his jacket pocket on school grounds," Simmons said.

The sheriff said the weapon had a full magazine.

The teenager was arrested on several charges, including possession of a firearm on school grounds, possession of a firearm by a minor, and offenses related to the fighting and possession of marijuana.

Simmons said deputies described fighting involving both parents and coaches.

"There were fights all over the place. There were coaches fighting. There were parents fighting," Simmons said. "This was a mess."

The violence prompted officials to cancel the remaining youth football games.

Simmons said his office subsequently learned of efforts to resume games at other locations, including Brent Ballpark and McGee Field.

The Sheriff's Office coordinated with county parks officials and Pensacola police to prevent further problems. Simmons said those games were canceled as well.

Authorities also received information about possible retaliation following the fights, although Simmons said he was not aware of any retaliation actually occurring.

The sheriff said organizers must ensure that youth sporting events can be conducted safely before scheduling additional games.

item.title: Kohler and Vinson Sworn In as Escambia County Commissioners
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County officially welcomed one new commissioner and returned another to office Tuesday morning, as Joe Vinson and Mike Kohler took their oaths during an installation ceremony at the Ernie Lee Magaha Government Building in downtown Pensacola. Vinson was sworn in as the new District 4 commissioner, while…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County officially welcomed one new commissioner and returned another to office Tuesday morning, as Joe Vinson and Mike Kohler took their oaths during an installation ceremony at the Ernie Lee Magaha Government Building in downtown Pensacola.

Vinson was sworn in as the new District 4 commissioner, while Kohler began another four-year term representing District 2 following his reelection earlier this month.

Both commissioners will serve terms extending through November 2030.

Kohler, who was joined by his family for the ceremony, thanked voters from across the political spectrum and promised to represent all residents of his district, regardless of how they voted.

"And so if you voted for me, I'm going to be your commissioner. And if you didn't, I'm going to be your commissioner, too, and I'm going to do everything I can for you," Kohler said.

Vinson kept his remarks brief, expressing appreciation for the opportunity to serve and encouraging residents to hold him accountable.

"Please hold my feet to the fire. Make sure that I do the things I say I'm going to do. And I look forward to serving you and working with you," Vinson told those attending.

Following the ceremony, commissioners unanimously approved Kohler's appointments to several county advisory boards.

Ross Padden will serve on the Board of Adjustment, William Van Horn on the Planning Board, and Charles Thornton on the Santa Rosa Island Authority. Clinton Retherford and Barry Johnson were also reappointed to the Escambia Marine Advisory Committee.

The appointments were approved by a 5–0 vote.

The ceremony marked the beginning of a new chapter for the commission as county leaders continue addressing hurricane recovery, budget uncertainty and the financial implications of Amendment 3.

item.title: HUD Cuts Off Funding to LA Homelessness Agency in Fraud Settlement
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced today that the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority will permanently lose federal funding under a landmark settlement resolving fraud allegations. LAHSA, which has received nearly $1 billion in HUD money over the past five years—more than any other jurisdiction in the nation—will be…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced today that the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority will permanently lose federal funding under a landmark settlement resolving fraud allegations. LAHSA, which has received nearly $1 billion in HUD money over the past five years—more than any other jurisdiction in the nation—will be required to return approximately $150 million and be severed from HUD's homelessness program by the end of 2027.

According to HUD, the agency's Office of Inspector General uncovered evidence of widespread fraud, mismanagement, and oversight failures at LAHSA. Despite receiving the largest share of federal homelessness funding nationwide, Los Angeles has seen homelessness increase and has become what HUD describes as the epicenter of the nation's drug-fueled homelessness crisis. HUD Secretary Marty Turner suspended LAHSA payments in June following the inspector general's findings.

Los Angeles County will assume responsibility for LAHSA's portfolio of projects and programs under strict HUD oversight. The settlement reflects the Trump administration's shift away from the "Housing First" approach toward what it calls "Treatment First" policies focused on addressing addiction and promoting self-sufficiency among unhoused populations.

For Pensacola and the broader Gulf Coast region, the case underscores the federal government's intensified scrutiny of homelessness spending and agencies managing those funds. Local nonprofits and government entities receiving HUD dollars should expect heightened compliance expectations and audit activity.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida will mark a significant milestone Thursday morning when it formally celebrates its selection as a Distinguished Military College by the U.S. Department of War and its admission into America's Corps of Cadets.

UWF President Manny Diaz Jr., along with Andrew Del Gaudio, executive director of the university's Office of Military Services, and other campus leaders will speak at the 10:30 a.m. event at the Argo Athletic Club on the Pensacola campus. The press conference will outline what the new designation means for UWF's academic mission and military community.

The selection places UWF among a select group of institutions recognized for their commitment to military education and training. The event takes place Thursday, November 19, at 11000 University Parkway.

item.title: Florida Preserves 50,000 Acres of Agricultural Land in Historic Milestone
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program has reached a historic milestone, with state officials announcing the preservation of more than 50,000 additional acres of working agricultural land, bringing the total permanently protected through the program to 308,000 acres, according to Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program has reached a historic milestone, with state officials announcing the preservation of more than 50,000 additional acres of working agricultural land, bringing the total permanently protected through the program to 308,000 acres, according to Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Commissioner Wilton Simpson.

The announcement came today as the Governor and Cabinet, acting as the Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund, approved the preservation actions. The easements prevent future development while allowing farms and ranches to continue operating on private land, maintaining agricultural production and contributing to Florida's economy. More than 243,000 of the total preserved acres have been protected during Simpson's tenure as commissioner.

One of the major projects approved is Osceola Prairie, a nearly 19,312-acre cattle and farming operation in Osceola County that will be preserved through a $77.75 million rural lands protection easement. The U.S. Department of Defense is contributing $15 million to the project. The property sits within the Kissimmee River Basin and Northern Everglades ecosystem and includes improved pasture, prairie, scrub, and wetlands, with seven center pivots for crop and hay production serving the cattle operation. It's also adjacent to conservation lands including Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park and the Kissimmee River Public Use Area.

All preserved properties are enrolled in the Florida Department of Agriculture's Best Management Practices and are located within the Florida Wildlife Corridor, a priority area established under state law in 2021.

item.title: ECPS Celebrates 34 Students Who Completed State Service Challenge
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools recognized 34 high school students Tuesday for completing the Student Service Challenge, a statewide initiative backed by the Florida Department of Education and Florida Lottery that promotes civic engagement and community service. Participating students from all seven ECPS high schools and Pensacola State College…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools recognized 34 high school students Tuesday for completing the Student Service Challenge, a statewide initiative backed by the Florida Department of Education and Florida Lottery that promotes civic engagement and community service.

Participating students from all seven ECPS high schools and Pensacola State College Charter Academy logged at least 20 hours of volunteer work between September 7 and October 5, volunteering with local organizations and helping people in need. Of the 40 students initially selected to participate, 34 successfully completed the program and submitted written reflections on how their service deepened their understanding of citizenship and leadership.

Each student received a $500 award funded through the Florida Lottery. Laura Touchstone, ECPS Director of High School Education, said the challenge reinforces a key lesson: "These students stepped outside of the classroom, identified needs within their communities, and took action." Superintendent Keith Leonard added that the program reflects the district's commitment to preparing students to be "engaged, compassionate citizens who understand the importance of giving back."

item.content:encoded: Radio and television broadcasts across the country, including in the Pensacola area, will be briefly interrupted today as federal officials conduct a scheduled test of the Emergency Alert System. The test, coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission, is set to begin at approximately 1:20 p.m. Viewers and listeners should expect to hear or see a message indicating the broadcast is only a test. The nationwide EAS test happens periodically to ensure the system functions properly in the event of an actual emergency.

item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has launched its annual sewer averaging period, which officially kicked off Sunday, November 15. During this time, ECUA uses customer water consumption data from the past 12 months to calculate a more stable sewer charge, rather than billing based on month-to-month fluctuations. For many households and…
item.content:encoded: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has launched its annual sewer averaging period, which officially kicked off Sunday, November 15. During this time, ECUA uses customer water consumption data from the past 12 months to calculate a more stable sewer charge, rather than billing based on month-to-month fluctuations. For many households and businesses in the ECUA service area — which covers parts of Escambia and Santa Rosa counties — this averaging approach can provide more predictable billing, especially for those whose water use varies seasonally. The utility typically uses this period to smooth out spikes from summer usage or other temporary consumption patterns, spreading costs more evenly across billing cycles. Customers who have questions about how the averaging period affects their specific accounts can contact ECUA directly for details on their individual calculations.

item.content:encoded:
The western portion of the new North Palafox Street bridge spanning Interstate 10 is scheduled to open this week, according to reporting on the I-10 at Highway 29 interchange improvement project in Escambia County.

The bridge opening marks a significant milestone in the ongoing effort to improve traffic flow and safety at one of the region's busiest highway intersections. The project has been designed to address capacity and congestion issues in the area serving commuters and commercial traffic.

This is the first phase of the bridge opening. Additional details about full project completion and the eastern portion timeline were not provided in the initial announcement.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is hosting a public meeting today to discuss a draft permit renewal for industrial injection wells at the Ascend Performance Materials facility in Cantonment.

The open house runs from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. at the facility. The meeting gives residents and stakeholders a chance to review the proposed permit and submit comments on the injection well operations.

Ascend Performance Materials, a chemical manufacturer, operates industrial injection wells at its Cantonment location. The permit renewal is part of the state's ongoing environmental oversight of injection well operations in the area.

item.title: Century considers charging youth sports leagues for field use, utilities
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Town of Century is weighing a new fee structure that would charge youth sports associations for utilities, field use, and other operational costs at town facilities — a move that could effectively shut down youth athletic programs in the community, according to nonprofit sports leaders. Currently, youth sports organizations operate in Century…
item.content:encoded:
The Town of Century is weighing a new fee structure that would charge youth sports associations for utilities, field use, and other operational costs at town facilities — a move that could effectively shut down youth athletic programs in the community, according to nonprofit sports leaders.

Currently, youth sports organizations operate in Century with little to no cost for using municipal fields and facilities. Under the proposed change, the town would begin billing nonprofits for expenses including utilities, maintenance, and supplies like toilet paper.

Youth sports leaders have warned town officials that the fees would be financially prohibitive for volunteer-run organizations and would likely force them to cease operations in Century. The groups say they lack the funding to absorb such costs while still keeping programs affordable and accessible for local families.

The proposal appears to stem from the town's efforts to manage municipal budgets and facility costs. No timeline for a decision has been announced, but the issue is expected to be discussed at upcoming town meetings.

item.content:encoded:
Buoy 42039 off Pensacola is reporting significant wave heights of 8.2 feet Tuesday, according to Florida Gulf Signal marine weather monitoring. Waves are running at a 7-second interval, with northeast winds at 25.3 knots and air temperatures around 69 degrees.

The elevated sea conditions may affect small craft and coastal activities in the area. Boaters and beachgoers should exercise caution and check updated marine forecasts before heading out.
